description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-core_task_lib-version-1.0.1.description:
Library core_task_lib version 1.0.1.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with basic task specifications that may be needed in most applications
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

rotation_z_end.description: Total rotation angle [rad] of the task frame about its own initial Z axis at the end of the path. The rotation is applied progressively, proportionally to the path coordinate s. Use 0 to keep the initial orientation

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (as defined in the robot model, e.g. URDF link or tcp_frame) that follows the spline

maxacc.description: Maximum acceleration of the normalized path coordinate s [1/s^2] used by the trapezoidal profile. The resulting Cartesian acceleration [m/s^2] is approximately maxacc times the length of the path

K_progress_bounds.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraints that keep the path coordinate s within [0, 1]. Larger values push s back into the range faster

K_position.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that makes the task frame position follow the spline. Larger values reduce the tracking error faster; too large values can cause oscillations or saturate the joint velocities

csv_file_path.description: Path of the CSV file (extension .csv) with the points that define the spline (4 columns: s in [0,1], X, Y, Z offsets [m]). Either an absolute path or a path of the form $[ros_package_name]/relative/path, which is resolved w.r.t. the share directory of that ROS 2 package

weight_progress_bounds.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the constraints that keep the path coordinate s within [0, 1], relative to the other constraints of the same priority

weight_progress_max_rate.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the weak constraint that pushes the path coordinate s to progress at the rate maxvel. Should stay small compared to the other weights

weight_progress_profile.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the constraint that imposes the trapezoidal velocity profile on the path coordinate s. A higher weight enforces the profile more strictly against the tracking constraints (a lower weight lets the progress slow down when the robot cannot track the path)

weight_rotation.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the orientation tracking constraint relative to the other constraints of the same priority (position tracking and path progress constraints). Only relative weights matter: a higher weight makes orientation tracking dominate when constraints conflict

weight_position.description: Weight (dimensionless) of the position tracking constraint relative to the other constraints of the same priority (orientation tracking and path progress constraints). Only relative weights matter: a higher weight makes position tracking dominate when constraints conflict

K_rotation.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that makes the task frame orientation follow the orientation profile. Larger values reduce the tracking error faster; too large values can cause oscillations or saturate the joint velocities

maxvel.description: Maximum rate of progress of the normalized path coordinate s [1/s] (s goes from 0 to 1 over the whole path), i.e. the inverse of the minimum time to traverse the path. The resulting Cartesian speed [m/s] is approximately maxvel times the length of the path

is-follow_spline.description:
Task Specification: follow_spline.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: Makes a task frame of the robot follow a cubic spline path fitted through position points read from a CSV file, starting from the pose of the task frame at the start of the task.
The CSV file has 4 columns (separated by commas, spaces or tabs) and no header: the first column is the normalized path coordinate s, increasing from 0 (start) to 1 (end); the other three are the X, Y, Z position offsets [m] of the path w.r.t. the initial position of the task frame, along the axes of the robot base frame (root frame of the robot model). The first point should be (0, 0, 0, 0) so that the path starts at the current position.
The progress along the path is a path coordinate s (feature variable) that follows a trapezoidal velocity profile in s, limited by maxvel/maxacc (expressed in units of s, i.e. 1/s and 1/s^2) and bounded to [0, 1]. Meanwhile the orientation rotates progressively (proportional to s) about the initial Z axis of the task frame by rotation_z_end (default 1.5708 rad, i.e. about 90 degrees).
No input channels are used. The task exits when s reaches the end of the path (s = 1). Outputs: time, the position (x_tf, y_tf, z_tf) [m] of the task frame w.r.t. the robot base frame, and progress_variable (s).
